text.text: Run a raise like a pipeline. Every investor has a stage, a next step and an expected amount; the round shows what is committed against the target.
List a target set of investors and research who fits.
Warm intros first; log every contact.
Move interested investors to Meeting, then Diligence.
Collect term sheets together, compare, and close.
This workspace tracks the process only. Terms and legal questions belong with your lawyer.
Update next steps on every active investor
A pitch is a story told in eight slides. The outline below is the order that investors expect; the notes under it say what each slide has to prove.
Problem: this is real, frequent and costly for a named kind of customer.
Solution: your product removes the cost, shown rather than described.
Traction: people already pay or return; give the trend, not one number.
Market: how many such customers exist and how you reach them.
Business model: how one customer turns into revenue, and what it costs to win them.
Team: why these people will out-learn everyone else on this problem.
Financials and use of funds: what the money buys and what it should change by the next round.
The ask: the amount, the timeline and what you want beyond cash.
Update this whenever shares are issued or options are granted.
